note:
Every person of this surname the archive can name, gathered from every record set it holds and from David's own MyHeritage tree — parish burials, headstones, reconstructed households, FamilySearch record hits, the Gologorica pedigree, the Eleven of Gračišće, the Omiš chart, the direct line, the namesakes, **people read straight off register images by eye where no index exists**, and 555 individuals harvested from the live tree on 8 September 2026. **Identity here is by record, not by resolved individual**: two entries may be one person, and where the archive knows they are it has merged them. Nothing here is new evidence — it is all of the evidence, in one list, for the first time. **The parish shown is the register the record was filmed from**, not the place a transcriber typed: it comes from resolving each record to its image, its film and the catalogue entry for that film. Where a film covers more than one parish it is attributed to the film's principal parish, and that is a real limit of the method.

**This list is rebuilt when the research moves.** People found by reading a register page rather than by searching an index are marked *Read off the register* — they are in no index anywhere, so the only way to find them again is this page. The nine Vodnjan additions of 9 September 2026 came out of the *Liber Copulatorum* that way.

warn:
**Living people are named, and nothing more.** This archive lists living relatives **by name only** — no date of birth, no address, no place of residence, no photograph — at David's decision, as the family member compiling it. Everyone else **on this list** is dead, or is held here as **possibly living**, and the difference is now tested rather than assumed. Until **22 September 2026** the living flag was set by hand, so it caught the relatives David knew to name and nobody else; testing the dates instead found **eight people born between 1931 and 1946 with no death recorded anywhere this archive can reach**.

**Five of them are held as possibly living** — name and place, no dates. **The dates this archive withholds are still held**; they are simply not printed, and they come back the moment a death is found.

rows.note:
**Buried at Svetvinčenat on 8 November 1812, aged fifty-four**, which puts his birth about 1758. **This household is at Šterna, not Svetvinčenat.** The FamilySearch index entry for Felice Anto (22 September 1778) carries the image ark **3:1:3QS7-899X-KXF4**, which resolves to **film 005497887, frame 627** — a different film from Svetvinčenat's 005497885. The act was read there on 21 September 2026:

> *«**Adì 27 9bre 1778. Copich.** Felice Ant.o figlio legitimo e naturale di **M.ro Bortolo De Franceschi**…»*

**That register is a different animal from Svetvinčenat's.** It is kept in **Italian, not Latin**, and every entry carries a **village name in its date heading** — Sterna, Cabotori, Copich — because the parish serves a scatter of hamlets. Bortolo's children were baptised at **Copich**.

The sister record confirms it: Mariana De Franceschi, February 1786, same father Bortolo, is indexed with the event place **«Sterna, Litorale Austriaco»** in as many words. *(doc.)*

**Šterna is in north-western Istria, near Buje — some seventy kilometres from Svetvinčenat.** These are not the castle-town family and must not be read as them.

rows.name: Maria Matthia De Franceschi
rows.note:
**The act, read off the leaf — not the index of it.** Frame 106 of the Svetvinčenat baptism register 1764–1791:

> *«**Anno Dni 1784 Die 4 Septembris.** Maria Matthia filia legitima, ac naturalis **Victorii, et Euphemiæ jugalium De Franceschi**, nata 3 currentis, hodie per me subscriptum baptizata. **Patrini fuere Stephanus Dubglich a Dimino, et Dna Antonia Fachinetti.**»*

**Born 3 September 1784, baptised 4 September.** Daughter of [[vittorio-de-franceschi-son-of-antonio]] and [[euphemia-de-franceschi-1783]] — and therefore **Antonio the bell-ringer's granddaughter**, the third generation of the name this archive can follow at the castle. *(doc.)*

Her godfather comes from **Dvigrad**; her godmother, *Dna Antonia Fachinetti*, carries the honorific and a name from the parish's gentry.

**This entry is what turns a marriage from inference into record.** Until it was read, «Vittorio × Euphemia» rested on the FamilySearch index of this same act — a transcription of a page nobody here had seen. *(doc.)*

rows.name: Antony De Franceski
rows.place: Willowbank, City of Ipswich, Queensland, Australia
rows.note:
**Anton Mario De Franceski**, born **21 August 1944 at Reutlingen** — the four-year-old who sailed with Zdravko and Ruža on the *General M B Stewart*. **He was their elder child, not their only one**: his sister **Petrica** was born at Horsham in the Wimmera nine years after they landed, and this archive did not know she existed until David asked why she was not here. The National Archives of Australia hold the household as one file: **NAA A11534, 58–60 — «DEFRANCESKI Zdravko DOB 2 April 1921; Ruza DOB 13 February 1922; Anton DOB 21 August 1944»**, which agrees to the day with the Reutlingen and Neuhausen residence lists and with IRO card 52852. His own arrival card is **NAA D4881, DE FRANCESKI ANTON MARIO — «Arrived Melbourne per General M B Stewart 13 April 1949»**, and it runs to 31 December 1976. That card is where the middle name comes from, and where the spelling does: **De Franceski**, with a space and no *c*, which is the spelling on this headstone and on his father's.

**The cemetery register says he was 56.** Born 21 August 1944 he was **54**, seven weeks short of fifty-five. Three documents — two German, one Australian — give the same birth date, and an age written into a burial register is the weakest of the four. [Logged as an open question](/open-questions/)

rows.note:
**This household is at Šterna, not Svetvinčenat.** The FamilySearch index entry for Felice Anto (22 September 1778) carries the image ark **3:1:3QS7-899X-KXF4**, which resolves to **film 005497887, frame 627** — a different film from Svetvinčenat's 005497885. The act was read there on 21 September 2026:

> *«**Adì 27 9bre 1778. Copich.** Felice Ant.o figlio legitimo e naturale di **M.ro Bortolo De Franceschi**…»*

**That register is a different animal from Svetvinčenat's.** It is kept in **Italian, not Latin**, and every entry carries a **village name in its date heading** — Sterna, Cabotori, Copich — because the parish serves a scatter of hamlets. Bortolo's children were baptised at **Copich**.

The sister record confirms it: Mariana De Franceschi, February 1786, same father Bortolo, is indexed with the event place **«Sterna, Litorale Austriaco»** in as many words. *(doc.)*

**Šterna is in north-western Istria, near Buje — some seventy kilometres from Svetvinčenat.** These are not the castle-town family and must not be read as them.

rows.name: Hedviga Blažević (Defranceski)
rows.note:
**A singer at the Hotel Therapia, Crikvenica** — family testimony, 10 September 2026, and the likeliest explanation of how a Senj woman met a Crikvenica man. Daughter of **Ljubomir «Ljubo» Blažević, 1892–1966**, and **Milka Lucia Papić, 1886–1971**. Born at Senj and died at Johannesburg, 30 October 2001, of cancer.

**Born 3 August 1926.** The archive carried two dates — 8 March and 3 August, a day and month transposed — and preferred neither. **David's own tree gives 3 August**, so that is what this archive now says, marked as coming from the tree rather than from a register. The Senj birth register of 1926 would settle it for good and is [on the errands](/errands/).

**And she did not go straight to Johannesburg.** The tree gives her **immigration in April 1975, from Zimbabwe** — Rhodesia as it then was, in the middle of its war. This archive has drawn her route as *Senj → Johannesburg* and there is a country in the middle of it that nobody had written down. She married again about 1973, and the tree names two later husbands: **Santou (Shemtov) Isaac Codron, 1913–1997**, and **Ladislav Carr**. Ivan stayed on his own coast and is buried at Senj; the divorce the family put at about 1969 now has a shape around it. *tree — not yet a document.*

rows.name: Gasparo De Franceschi
rows.note:
**He was a twin, and the register proves it.** Image 116 of *Births 1709–1764* (film 005497885), read on the plate 23 September 2026: *«baptizavit **duos infantulos geminos natos hodie mane a Jacobo de Franceschi, et Anzola ejus legitima uxore**, quibus fuit positum nomen, uni […] alteri **Antonij**»*. **The index knew his name and not his brother; the plate knew his brother and not his name.** His twin is [[antonio-di-jacobo-de-franceschi-twin-1737]]. *(doc for the twinship; the forename is the index's.)*

«Casparg, of **Jacobo De Franceschi and Anzola**, 26 December 1737» — Giacomo's son by his second wife.

**⚠ The 1773 widow is not his. See [[gasparo-defranceschi-husband-of-maria-fl-1744]]** — *«Maria uxor Caspari Defranceschi»* stands godmother on **5 May 1744**, when this Gasparo was six years old and the other candidate eleven. **A third and older Gasparo was married by 1744, and the 1773 widow Maria is his.** *The paragraph below weighed two boys against each other and is left standing as the reasoning it was.*

**A Gasparo de Franceschi was dead before 30 March 1773.** On that day the marriage register records *«Joannes Volge, et **Maria relicta q.m Gasparis de Franceschi**»* — his widow remarrying, with a dispensation to marry in Lent and all three banns waived. **He would have been thirty-five — but he is not the only candidate.** The castle also holds **Domenico Gasparo, son of Giacomo, baptised 9 August 1732**, who was still alive in February 1764, standing godfather as *«D. Gasparo de Franceschi figlio di Giacomo»*, and who would have been forty-one in 1773. **Two men of the name, one generation, either of whom fits.** The 1773 entry gives no father and no age, so the death is recorded as a possibility against both and as neither man's fact. *(inf; the death itself is doc.)* See [/searched/](/searched/).

**He is named as Giacomo's son, twice, in 1762.** *«Gasparo figlio di M.o Giacomo de Franceschi»* stands godfather on **1 August** and **15 December 1762** — both magnified. At twenty-four he is exactly the age this dossier's 1737 baptism would predict, and the two records corroborate each other across twenty-five years. *(inf, and the firmest thing on this page.)*

**It also removes a phantom.** Entries of 1751–1761 naming a «Gasparo De Franceschi» as godfather, and a «Pasqua moglie di Gasparo de Franceschi» as godmother, had been read here as a second household beside Giacomo's. They are the same house.

rows.name: Fosca De Franceschi
rows.note:
«Dominicus Defranceschi, et **Fosca** Uxor ejus», godparents at Svetvinčenat on **16 April 1780**.

**And again at the end of the following year.** Carta 90, **31 December 1781**: *«Patrini ac sacro fonte fuere Joannes Baptista Mischanic, et **Jusca uxor Dominici** [De]franceschi»* — godmother to a daughter of Joannes Pribcovich. **The register writes her «Jusca» here and «Fosca» in 1780**, which is one woman and two ears.

*(doc — the given names were read at magnification; the surname at spread scale, against a man independently attested twice in the same volume.)* Read 21 September 2026, film 005497885, image 93.

**Five more appearances, all magnified, all in the same hand.** The sweep of frames 90–107 found her at the font again and again:

| date | frame | how the clerk wrote her |
|---|---|---|
| 9 September 1781 | 91 | «Mattheus Bursich, vulgo Petrovich, et **Fosca Vxor Dominici Defranceschi**» |
| 20 September 1782 | 98 | «Victorius filius Antonii de Franceschi, et **Fosca Vxor Dominici Defranceschi**» |
| 10 December 1782 | 99 | «Nicolaus Fabri, et **Fvsca Vxor Dominici De-Franceschi**» |
| 16 December 1783 | 102 | «Matthaeus Doblanovich, et **Fvsca Vxor Dominici de Franceschi**» |
| 3 January 1784 | 102 | «Matthaeus Cossa, et **Fvsca Vxor Dominici de Franceschi**» |

**Seven attestations now, 1780 to 1784.** She is one of the parish's standing godmothers — the woman a family asked for when it wanted someone of weight at the font. *(doc; every line above read at magnification.)*

**A caution that belongs on this page.** Frame 98 also carries *«et **Fosca Vxor Martini Merklem**»* — a different Fosca entirely, four entries above our own. **Fosca is a common forename in this parish, not a rare one.** Only the full form *«Fosca uxor Dominici Defranceschi»* identifies her; a bare «Fosca» identifies nobody. *(This archive nearly wrote down the wrong woman.)*

**An eighth appearance, and a correction to how it was first read.** Frame 112, **13 December 1785**: *«Patrini fuere **Victorivs de Franceschi, et Fvsca Vxor Dominici de Franceschi**»*. At spread scale the first godparent was read as *Antonius*; **magnified it is Victorius** — Vittorio, not his father. *(doc.)*

**Five spellings, one woman — and the list is worth setting out, because a careless reader would make three people of her.** Across 1780–1789 the register writes Domenico's wife as:

**Fosca** (1780, 1781, 1782) · **Fusca** (1782–86) · **Jusca** (1782, 1788) · **Justa** (1788) · **Julia** (1789)

Every one of them is *«uxor Dominici Defranceschi»*, in a parish with one Domenico of the name. **No remarriage is implied by any of them, and none should be inferred.** The variation is the clerk's ear, not the household's history. *(doc for the entries; the identification across spellings is inf, and firm.)*

rows.name: Mathea De Franceschi
rows.note:
«**Mathea** uxor Antonij Defranceschi», godmother at Svetvinčenat on **1 May 1780**.

**And she is still alive two years later.** Frame 98 of the same volume, **18 August 1782**: *«Patrini ad sacrum fontem fuere Martinus Merklem, et **Matthea Vxor Antonij Defranceschi**»* — godmother to Maria, daughter of Georgius Piglich and Lucia. Magnified. **Her attested span is now 1 May 1780 to 18 August 1782**, and her husband is alive alongside her. *(doc.)*

rows.name: Francisca Matthaea Defranceschi
rows.note: «Francisca Matthæa» in the register. **Born 10 October 1747, baptised 13 October**, a daughter of **Valentino Defranceschi** and **Helena/Elena**, on **image 146 of film 005497925** (`3:1:3QS7-L99F-W44W`). **She is in no index anywhere**, and unlike the other four unindexed children of this household **nothing pointed at her** — she was found by sweeping the 1746–1750 gap frame by frame looking for a son. **The sixteenth child**, and the one that ends the claim that the household fell silent for five years. See [Valentino's sixteen](/fiume-1626/#valentino).

rows.name: Josephus Aloysius de Franceschi
rows.note: **Born 24 May 1748, baptised 29 May**, son of **D.nus Joannes Baptista de Franceschi** and **D.na Magdalena**, on **image 150 of film 005497925** (`3:1:3QS7-L99F-W4CK`). **In no index anywhere.** He is **almost certainly the Giuseppe Defranceschi b. 1748, d. 1778** the MyHeritage tree already carries at Rijeka without a source — the **Giuseppe × Francesca** who baptised four children at Fiume between 1772 and 1778 and whose son Valentino heads the Rijeka chain. *(inf — no entry names his father in 1772.)* His parents put him in a **second Fiume Defranceschi household**, not Valentino the Carnian's.

rows.name: Joannes Baptista de Franceschi
rows.note: **The head of the second Defranceschi household at Fiume.** Styled *D.nus*, married to **D.na Magdalena**, he baptises **Josephus Aloysius on 29 May 1748** (film 005497925, image 150). By **9 December 1771** he is a **widower**, marrying **Catharina de Benzoni** (film 005497925, volume 2, image 293), and has indexed children by her in **1773** and **1776**. **He is not one of Valentino the Carnian's sons** — the only *Joannes Baptista* among them was baptised in 1751. How the two households are related is unanswered; their **marriage entries are on the same reel**, in volume 1's marriages of 1734–1753.

rows.name: Elena Surcho (Defranceschi)
rows.note:
**Valentino the Carnian's wife, under her own name.** She married **«D.num Valentinum de Franceschi ex Carnia»** at St Vitus, Fiume on **28 February 1737** (film 005497925, image 168), nine months before their first child, and bore **sixteen children** to 1757. Every other entry in twenty years calls her only *Helena* or *Elena jugalis Defranceschi*; **this is the one document that gives her a maiden name.** *(The surname is underlined in the register; its initial is the looped capital this hand uses for both S and Z, so **Surcho**, **Zurcho** or **Turcho** — probably an Italianised Žurko/Zurco. Given as read.)* She stands godmother across the parish at least **nine times** between 1745 and 1747, and again at the font of **Giuseppe × Francesca's** first son in 1772.

*(22 Sept 2026 — magnified. The body of the word is plainly **-urcho**; only the capital is in doubt. **Turcho** was added to the list because *Turco/Turcho* is a common Adriatic surname and *Surcho* is not. None of the three is preferred.)*

rows.name: Maria di Nardo Defranceschi
rows.note:
**«Maria d' m.ro **Nardo defranceschi** 13 Agosto 1709 — c. 13 tergo»**, from the **M** page of the Svetvinčenat births index, 1709–1764 (film 005497884, index image 204).

**Her father is the Nardo this archive already met.** The 1707 register carries a boy **Piero baptised twice**, on 6 and 15 October, to a father written **Nardo** once and **Lunardo** once and a mother **Eufemia** both times. **This is that household two years on**, and it is the first thing this archive has found at Svetvinčenat **after 1707** — which is exactly where its reading stopped.

*The «m.ro» is the trade title* — *maestro* — which the Svetvinčenat fathers of this name carry from 1666 onward. **Carta 13 t° is unopened**, and would give the mother and the godparents. *(doc for the index line; the register leaf is unread.)*

rows.note: **This row and the index row are the same child.** The index entry that first put her here (*«Marina di Piero Defranceschi, 21 Febraro 1710 — c. 6»*) and the leaf are merged: the leaf wins on the carta and adds the mother.*22 September 2026 — the index entry behind this reading is now attached: **`1:1:X9DP-3HTQ`**, *«Marina De Franceschi · Baptism 1710 · Croazia, Austria · Father **Piero De Franceschi** · Mother **Vittoria**»*. **The mother's name is new** — the page gave the father and not her. The eye-read and the index agree on everything else, which is worth having said.*

rows.name: Maria di Batta Defranceschi
rows.note:
**«Maria di Batto Defranceschi, 13 Luglio 1716 — c. 26»**, from the **M** page of the Svetvinčenat births index, 1709–1764 (film 005497884, index image 205).

**She is the earliest child of Batta's household this archive holds.** *Batta* — Gio Batta, Giovanni Battista — was known here for **Gasparo (10 August 1718)**, **Cattarina (10 February 1728)** and **Battistina (1731)**. **Maria of 1716 comes two years before Gasparo** and pushes the household back.

**Carta 26 is unopened**, and would give the mother — which matters, because carta 66 gives Batta's wife as **Anzoletta** in 1728 while the families page carries a *«1733 Maria, of **Giacomo** and Anzoletta»*. **Two husbands for one wife's name, and this entry is twelve years earlier than either.** *(doc for the index line; the register leaf is unread.)*

**Flagged, 21 September 2026: carta 26 has been opened and she is not on it.** The leaf runs **18 April to 22 June 1716** and carries no Defranceschi; its verso opens on 18 July. **The index's «13 Luglio 1716 — c. 26» has nothing behind it at that carta.** She may still be real — a leaf either side would hold mid-July — but [she is now unlocated](/searched/), not confirmed. *(inf.)*

rows.name: Maria di Giacomo Defranceschi (1728)
rows.note:
**«Maria di Giacomo Defranceschi 11 Feb.o 1728 — c. 66»**, from the Svetvinčenat births index (film 005497884, «Matična knjiga rodjenih 1703–1763»). *(doc for the index line; the register leaf is unread.)*

**This settles a question the archive had open.** The families page carried *«1733 Maria, of **Giacomo** and Anzoletta»* while carta 66 gave *«**Batta** de Fran.chi et di Anzoletta»* in 1728 — **two husbands for one forename**. The index shows why: **carta 66 carries both**. Batta's **Cattarina on 10 February 1728** and Giacomo's **Maria on 11 February 1728**, *one day apart on the same leaf*. **They are two different men.** A reading of that leaf could very easily carry Anzoletta from one entry to the next.

rows.name: Maria di Giacomo Defranceschi (1733)
rows.note:
**«Maria di Giacomo Defranceschi 4 9bre 1733 — c. 83»**, from the Svetvinčenat births index (film 005497884, «Matična knjiga rodjenih 1703–1763»). *(doc for the index line; the register leaf is unread.)*

**Giacomo's second Maria.** The first was baptised **11 February 1728** (carta 66). A family that uses a name twice has usually buried the first child — the same pattern this archive found at Fiume, where Giuseppe's Valentino of 1772 died in 1775 and the next son was christened Valentino again in 1776. **This is the Maria the families page dates to 1733**, and the date was right.

rows.name: Piero di Nadal Defranceschi (1734)

rows.name: Nadal Defranceschi
rows.note:
**A third Defranceschi household in the castle, and he is here only as a father.** The **P** page of the Svetvinčenat births index names him twice — **«Piero di Nadal Defranceschi»** about **1725** and again on **12 February 1734**. *Nadal* is **Natale**, and he is **not** the *Nardo* (Leonardo) who fathered Piero in 1707 and Maria in 1709.

**So by the 1730s the castle holds at least five men of the name fathering children** — **Nardo**, **Piero**, **Batta**, **Giacomo** and **Nadal** — which is what the *Atti* meant by calling this the one surname with a continuity in San Vincenti. *(inf — named in records, with none of his own yet.)*

**He steps out of the index and onto a leaf.** On **12 July 1732**, carta 79 verso, *«Padrini al S. Fonte furono **D. Nadal Defraneschi**»* — godfather to Valentin, son of Micò Vitich, **with the honorific D.** **Beware the same leaf**: four entries below him a godmother is entered as *«Maria mog. di **Nadal Venir**»*, a different man and a different family. *(doc.)*

**The Antonio she is married to is almost certainly the Antonio of *Atti* 48** — *«Guidati da Antonio Defranceschi, nel 1780 avevano ottenuto l'esonero dal partecipare alla difesa armata»* — same castle, same year. **This archive does not merge them**: the register gives a husband's forename and the article gives a leader's, and nothing yet joins the two documents. *(doc for the entry; inf for the identification.)*

Read off the leaf, 21 September 2026 — film 005497885, births 1764–1791, frame 81.

rows.name: Elena De Franceschi (Sandalezza)
rows.note:
**Married 9 February 1766 at San Vincenti**, and the first marriage of this name the archive has read there. *«…ha contratto il matrimonio per verba de presenti con **Elena figlia di q. Mattio de Franceschi, nativa di questo Castello**»* — carta 11 of the marriages 1762–1815.

**Her husband is Mattio, son of the late Michiel Sandalezza**, a native of the **Territory of Albona** (Labin) who had lived about **fifteen years** in the district of San Vincenti before he was admitted to marry here.

**Her father was already dead.** A bride of 1766 was born around the 1740s — inside the twenty-nine years [the volume's index cannot reach](/searched/). *(doc, read at magnification, 21 September 2026.)*

rows.name: Mattio De Franceschi
rows.note:
**Dead before 9 February 1766**, and known only because his daughter married. The marriage entry calls her *«Elena figlia di **q[uondam] Mattio de Franceschi**, nativa di questo Castello»* — *quondam* being the whole of what is recorded about him.

**He is the ninth man of the name at the castle** and no birth, marriage or burial of his has been found. **This archive already carries a Mattio De Franceschi born 1674 and another born 1690 at Svetvinčenat**, from the household and tree sources. **A man dying before 1766 could be either, or neither, and none of the three is merged here** — the marriage gives a forename and a death-before date, which is not enough to join a person to a person. *(doc for the fact of his death; the identification is open.)*

**He has a second daughter, and so his household has a shape.** On 17 October 1773 the same register marries *«**Fusca filia q. Mathiae de Franceschi** Parochiana huius Ecclesiae»* to Marc'Antonio Jacomini. **Elena in 1766 and [[fusca-de-franceschi]] in 1773 are both daughters of a dead Mattio de Franceschi of this parish** — two entries, seven years apart, in one volume. *(doc for each entry; that the two fathers are one man is inf, and it would take two dead Mattios in one small parish to break it.)* He remains recorded only through his children's weddings.

rows.name: Marie Defranceschi
rows.note:
**The only woman of the name yet found in Lorraine, and her own daughter's birth act spells her differently from the record that led here.** David brought a French *Table des successions et absences* naming **Marie DEFRANCESKI**, widow of **Louis Alphonse LABAYE**, who died at **Bénaménil (Meurthe-et-Moselle)** on **4 April 1940**. Two censuses and a decennial table later, the couple is documented — under the spelling **Defranceschi**.

The **1910 birth register of Thiébauménil**, the commune next to Bénaménil, opens its year with her child (*2 E 519/7, image 170; acte n° 1*):

> *«L'an mil neuf cent dix, le **trente janvier à onze heures du matin**. Pardevant Nous, **Nicolas Joseph Roi**, Maire et Officier de l'État civil de la commune de **Thiébauménil**, arrondissement de Lunéville […] a comparu : **Louis Alphonse Labaye, âgé de ~~cinquante~~ quarante-un ans, domicilié à Thiébauménil, maçon**, lequel nous a déclaré qu'aujourd'hui à huit heures du matin, **Marie Defranceschi, âgée de vingt-neuf ans, sans profession, son épouse**, est accouchée en son domicile d'un enfant du sexe **féminin** […] les prénoms de **Marthe Louise**.»*

**Aged twenty-nine in January 1910, so born about 1880 or 1881.** Her husband was a mason, forty-one, born about 1868 — which is exactly the birth year the succession table estimated thirty years later. *(doc.)*

**Two daughters, both born at Thiébauménil**, from the commune's decennial table *(2 E 519/TD 2, images 36–37, a typed table printed 27 November 1995)*: **Henriette Amélie**, acte 8 of **11 July 1908**, and **Marthe Louise**, acte 1 of **30 January 1910**. A margin note on Marthe's act carries her forward: *«Mariée à Bénaménil le 19 mai 1934 avec Ernest Larger»* — and the **1936 census of Bénaménil** duly lists *«Labaye Marthe 1910 Thiébauménil»* as the wife of *Larger Ernest, peintre*, with their daughter *Rose, 1927*. *(doc.)*

**Where Marie came from is still open.** The couple did **not** marry at Thiébauménil: its marriage table for 1903–1912 runs *Humbert Jean Charles → Leybach Constant Lucien* with no Labaye, and carries no Defranceschi under her own name either. The marriage act — the one record that would give her parents and her birthplace — is in some other commune's register. *(inf, for the negative.)*

rows.name: Giacomo de Franceschi (d. bef. 1771)
rows.note:
**Dead before 23 November 1771**, and on the page only as a word: *quondam*. A marriage witness that day is entered as *«Jacobo **q. Jacobi de Franceschi**»* — Giacomo, son of the late Giacomo de Franceschi. Nothing else of him is recorded there: no age, no trade, no widow.

**He is the tenth man of the name at the castle**, and he may not be a tenth man at all — this archive already holds a **Giacomo De Franceschi born 1706** and another **born 1731** at Svetvinčenat, and the father of a man marrying in 1772 could be either. **None of the three is merged here.** *(doc for the fact of his death; the identification is open.)* See [[giacomo-de-franceschi-m-1772]].

**His household is now partly visible.** Four baptisms between 1750 and 1759 give a **Giacomo de Franceschi** and **Pascasia** as parents at this parish — the children being an unread forename (1750), Giacomo Battista (1753), Giovanni (1756) and Antonia (1759). **Whether that Giacomo is this one is open**: the register also carries a *«Jacobus filius Jacobi Defranceschi»* standing godfather in 1754, and godmothers styled *«uxor Jacobi Defranceschi»* whose forename reads as *Veneranda* rather than *Pascasia* in 1754, 1755 and 1756. **Either two men of the name were married at once, or those three lines are misread at scan resolution; they have not yet been magnified.** *(inf, and flagged.)*

**He had a grown son called Gasparo, and that collapses two households into one.** Twice in 1762 the baptism register writes *«**Gasparo figlio di M.o Giacomo de Franceschi**»* — 1 August and 15 December, both magnified. This archive had been reading Gasparo and Giacomo as two separate households running alongside each other through the 1750s; they are a father and his adult son. *(doc.)*

**And the volume's own index dates that son.** It carries *«Casparg, of Jacobo De Franceschi and Anzola, 26 December 1737»* — which makes Gasparo **twenty-four** in August 1762, exactly the age of an adult godparent. **So Giacomo married twice: Anzola, mother of Gasparo, and Pascasia, mother of the four children of 1750–1759.** *(inf, from two records twenty-five years apart.)*

rows.name: Giacomo de Franceschi (m. 1772)
rows.note:
**Married at Svetvinčenat on 10 June 1772** — the first wedding of the name found in the parish's marriage register, which no one had opened before this archive did.

> *«Anno Domini 1772, 10 Junij. **Giacobus filius Giacobi de Franceschi**, et **Nicolina filia Nicolai Teserati**, juncti sunt per verba de presenti per me D. Martinum Luciani ex comissione Parochi, tribus premissis denunciationibus, testibus D.no Michaele Luciani et Vicentio Vemir alijsque pluribus, addita benedictione.»*

**He appears seven months earlier as a witness**, on 23 November 1771, where the clerk is more careful and writes *«Jacobo **q.** Jacobi de Franceschi»* — so his father was already dead. A man marrying in 1772 was most likely born in the 1740s, which is exactly the stretch the parish's baptism index does not reach. **No baptism of his has been found and he is merged with nobody.** *(doc for the marriage; the birth is inferred and the identification open.)* The bride's surname is the one word on the page this reading will not guarantee — **Teserati**, possibly *Teseveti*.

**A candidate for who he was.** The baptism register has a **Giacomo Battista, son of Giacomo Defranceschi and Pascasia, born 19 August 1753** — eighteen at the time of this wedding, and eighteen when his father died. **The fit is good and it is not claimed**, because the same register shows a second, older *«Jacobus filius Jacobi Defranceschi»* as a godfather in May 1754, so there were already two men of the forename in the same generation. *(inf.)* See [[giacomo-battista-de-franceschi-b-1753]].

rows.name: Antonio de Franceschi (witness 1773)
rows.note:
**Named six times in ten months of 1773, and never as a bridegroom — always as the man the parish asked to stand witness.** On 25 January, twice on 27 January, on 2 May, on 5 August and on 31 October 1773 the Svetvinčenat marriage register closes the entry *«testibus **Ant.º de Franceschi** et Jo: Sain»*, or the same with Vincentio Vemir or Stephano Petrovich in Sain's place.

**He has a grown son.** On 4 February 1773 the witness is *«**Victorio de Franceschi filio Antonij**»* — Vittorio, son of Antonio. That single phrase is what dates him: a son old enough to witness in 1773 puts Antonio's own birth **about 1730 at the latest**, and possibly a decade earlier. *(doc for the appearances and for the son; the birth year is inferred from his son's age.)*

**He is not merged with anyone.** The archive already carries an **Antonio De Franceschi born 1704** at Svetvinčenat, who would have been sixty-nine in 1773 — possible, and not proven. A name and a decade is not an identification. See [[vittorio-de-franceschi-son-of-antonio]].

**He was the bell-ringer, and that is why he is on so many pages.** Three entries of 1774–75 give him an occupation, one of them with the word in front where it cannot be misparsed: *«e del **Campanaro Antonio Defranceschi**»* (25 September 1775), *«**Ant.º Defranceschi Campanaro**, ed altri»* (27 February 1775), *«d'**Ant.º Defranceschi Campanaro**»* (29 October 1775). **This archive first read his six 1773 appearances as a mark of standing. The duller explanation is the right one: he worked at the church, and the priest reaching for a witness reached for the man already in the building.** *(doc.)*

**He does not hold the title alone.** *«Zne Sain Campanaro»* appears in February and July 1776 and January 1777. Either the office changed hands or the parish had more than one bell-ringer. *(inf.)*

**Eleven appearances in all, 1773 to 1775**, and then nothing: after 1775 the name in the witness line is **Domenico**. See [[domenico-defranceschi-witness-1777]].

**His own marriage is not in the book.** The whole volume, 1762–1779, has now been read frame by frame. With a son old enough to witness in February 1773 he married about 1750–1756, before this register opens — inside the gap between 1623 and 1762 that the parish's marriage books do not cover. *(doc, for the negative.)*

**He is a grandfather in the record too.** His son Vittorio's children are in this archive's burials: Antonia (1804–1808), Giovanni Pietro (1809), **Antonio (1811)** and Gioanni Maria (d. 1813). The grandson carries his name, which is what the parish's naming habit would predict. *(inf.)* **Three generations of the name at Svetvinčenat now run Antonio → Vittorio → Antonio**, on the strength of a witness line, a burial and a naming pattern — no baptism among them.

**And here he is as a father, which is what eight days of reading were for.** The baptism register of 1764–1791, at **9 December 1769**, carta 26: *«**Fran.ca figlia di D.no Ant.o De Franceschi** e Donna **Mattia** … nata li 8 corrente»*. Magnified and read letter by letter.

**So Antonio was a householder at Svetvinčenat by 1769** — not a man who arrived about 1770, which is what this archive had been inferring from his absence as a parent in volume one. He is styled **D.no**, Dominus, a courtesy the register withholds from most of the parish. *(doc.)*

**His wife is Mattia — the Matthea who stands godmother in 1780** as *«Matthea uxor Antonij Defranceschi»*. *(doc for both entries; the household is inf.)* Their children, so far: **[[vittorio-de-franceschi-son-of-antonio]]** (b. about 1758) and **[[franca-de-franceschi-b-1769]]** (b. 8 December 1769).

**A second daughter, and she was a twin.** On **21 January 1776** the register has *«Dom[enic]a filia legit[i]ma et natu[rali]s D[omi]ni Antonij Defranceschi, Matthæque ejus [conjugis], **nata gemina** hac nocte elapsa»* — magnified. **[[domenica-de-franceschi-b-1776]]** joins Franca (1769) and Vittorio (c. 1758) as his children. The twin has not been found. *(doc.)*

**A fifth child, found in somebody else's baptism.** Frame 112, **18 January 1786**: *«Patrini fuere Matthaeus Doblanovich, et **Maria filia Antonii de Franceschi**»*. Magnified. **[[maria-de-franceschi-daughter-of-antonio]]** joins Vittorio, Franca, Domenica and Domenico. **Her own baptism has not been found**, and no birth year is inferred for her. *(doc for the daughter; her age is open.)*

**His children now stand at the font in his place.** By 1785–86 it is Vittorio, Vittorio's wife Euphemia, and Maria whose names fill the godparent line — the same office Antonio himself held through the 1770s.

**And he is still alive in 1788.** Frame 123, **12 October 1788**: *«Patrini fuere **Antonivs Defranceschi**, et Helena uxor Dni Benedicti Fiorencij»* — godfather to Martinus, son of Joannes and Catharina Xivolich. Magnified.

He was last seen in person on 10 September 1783. **This adds five years.** If he was born about 1730 — which his son's age in 1773 requires — he is about fifty-eight here. *(doc for the entry.)*

**The identification is inference, and narrow inference.** The entry says *«an Antonio Defranceschi»*, not *«the»*. But the only other men of that name this archive places at the castle are his own grandson, born 1811 and not yet alive, and an Antonio of 1671 long dead. **No other candidate exists in the parish in 1788.** *(inf.)*

rows.name: Vittorio de Franceschi (son of Antonio)
rows.note:
**The first father-and-son pair of the name this archive can document at Svetvinčenat.** At the wedding of Michael Sarcovich and Maria Crisman on **4 February 1773** the witnesses are entered as *«Jo: Sain, et **Victorio de Franceschi filio Antonij**»*.

Nothing else is said of him — no age, no trade, no wife. **What the entry is worth is the word *filio*:** it ties him to [[antonio-de-franceschi-witness-1773]], who was standing witness at the same altar six other times that year. *(doc.)*

**A probable identification, left open.** This archive carries a **Vittorio Defranceschi, 1758–1812**, the only Vittorio at the castle, known from his burial. He would have been fifteen in February 1773 — young, though *«filio Antonij»* is precisely how a clerk distinguishes a young man from his father. **The two are not merged.** *(inf.)*

**The identification is no longer open, and the evidence was in this archive's own files.** `burials.json` carries: **Vitorio Defranceschi, born 1758, died and buried 8 November 1812, aged 54, Svetvinčenat, kin: Antonio.** The 1773 register says *«filio Antonij»*; the 1812 burial says *kin: Antonio*. **Two independent records thirty-nine years apart give the same man of the same parish the same father.** *(doc.)*

**A third thing points the same way.** His own children are in the same file — **Antonia** (1804–1808), **Giovanni Pietro** (1809), **Antonio** (1811), **Gioanni Maria** (d. 1813). In a parish that names the first son for the paternal grandfather, a Vittorio who calls a son **Antonio** is a Vittorio whose father was Antonio. *(inf.)*

**His baptism has not been found, and the search is bounded.** Images 171–181 of the baptism register cover 1756 to 1760 continuously and hold no Defranceschi child of any Antonio — and 1758 is inside that stretch. The volume's own index stops around 1736 and cannot help. **Images 155–170 (1750–1756) and 182–196 (1761–1763) are still unread.** *(doc, for the negative.)*

**He becomes a father himself.** The FamilySearch index carries *«**Maria Matthia De Franceschi**, 3 September 1784, parents **Victorii De Franceschi & Euphemię**»* — Vittorio at twenty-six, with a wife **Euphemia**, and a daughter who carries his mother's name, **Matthia**. *(index; the act has not yet been read on the page.)*

**And he has a sister.** [[franca-de-franceschi-b-1769]] was baptised 9 December 1769 as *«figlia di D.no Ant.o De Franceschi»* — eleven years his junior. *(inf, on a shared father's name, parish and decade.)*

**A second *«filius Antonij»*, nine years after the first.** Frame 98, **20 September 1782**: *«Patrini qui susceperunt fuere **Victorius filius Antonii de Franceschi**, et Fosca Vxor Dominici Defranceschi»*. Magnified. **Two independent register entries, 1773 and 1782, give him the same father in the same words** — and the 1812 burial's `kin: Antonio` makes three. *(doc.)*

**By 1784 he needs no father to identify him.** Frame 103, **8 May 1784**: *«Patrini fuere **Victorivs de Franceschi**, et Constantia Vxor Antonij Fabri»* — godfather to Helena, daughter of Matthaeus and Justina Millovan, with no *filius* attached. At about twenty-six he is a man the clerk names on his own account. *(doc.)*

**His wife is named on the page, not just in an index.** Frame 110, **22 August 1785**: *«Patrini fuere Antonius Radocovich, et **Evphemia Vxor Victoris de Franceschi**»* — magnified. Until this line, «Vittorio × Euphemia» rested entirely on the FamilySearch *index* of his daughter Maria Matthia's 1784 baptism. **The register now says it in its own hand.** *(doc.)* See [[euphemia-de-franceschi-1783]].

**And he is on these pages constantly by the mid-1780s**: godfather on **30 July 1785** (*«Victorivs de Franceschi, et Helena Vxor Dni Benedicti Fiornzas»*) and again on **13 December 1785** alongside Fosca (*«Victorivs de Franceschi, et Fusca Vxor Dominici de Franceschi»*), both magnified. At about twenty-seven he has taken over the role his father held a decade earlier.

***«Victorius filius Antonii de Franceschi»* — a third time, in 1787.** Frame 119, **30 June 1787**, godfather to Joanna daughter of Michael and Catharina Duchenez, alongside *«Jacoba uxor Matthei Bergamo»*. Magnified.

**The father-and-son link now rests on four independent records spanning thirty-nine years**: the marriage-witness line of 4 February 1773, the baptisms of 20 September 1782 and 30 June 1787, and the burial of 8 November 1812 with its `kin: Antonio`. *(doc.)*

**He stands at the font throughout the 1780s** — 8 May 1784, 30 July and 13 December 1785, 8 March 1786, 4 May and 30 November 1787, twice in March 1788, 26 December 1788, 6 September 1789, 5 August 1790, 15 December 1790. **The whole 1764–1791 volume has now been read opening by opening**, and across it Vittorio is the single most frequently named man of the surname. *(doc.)*

rows.name: Fusca de Franceschi
rows.note:
**Married Marc'Antonio Jacomini at Svetvinčenat on 17 October 1773**, and in doing so gave this archive its first pair of siblings of the name at the castle-town.

> *«Mar[c]-Antonius Jacomini filius Andreae … et **Fusca filia q. Mathiae de Franceschi** Parochiana huius Ecclesiae, dispensatis a denunciationibus, per verba de presenti … per me D. Michaele Luciani ex commissione Parochi, addita B[enedictio]ne, **Testes D. Antonius de Franceschi, ac Mathias Santalera**.»*

**Seven years earlier, in the same register, Elena married as *«figlia di q. Mattio de Franceschi»*.** Same dead father, same parish. **Fusca and [[elena-de-franceschi-sandalezza]] are sisters** — the joining is inference, but it would take two dead Mattios de Franceschi in one small parish to break it. *(doc for the marriage; inf for the sisterhood.)*

**Antonio the bell-ringer stands witness at her wedding**, which is the closest thing the register offers to a link between the two households of the name. It is not a statement of kinship and is not treated as one. See [[antonio-de-franceschi-witness-1773]] and [[mattio-de-franceschi]].

rows.name: Domenico Defranceschi (witness 1777)
rows.note:
**Twice in one day, 29 November 1777, and standing exactly where Antonio used to stand.** The Svetvinčenat marriage register closes two weddings that day with *«alla presenza mia di Simon Manzoni e **Dom.co Defranceschi**»* and *«presenza di **Dom.co Defranceschi** e di Simon Manzoni»* — the same Simon Manzoni who had partnered [[antonio-de-franceschi-witness-1773]] at the altar in 1775.

**Antonio is not named in the register again after 1775; Domenico appears in 1777.** That is a handover in shape, and nothing more — the entries state no relationship and give Domenico no age, trade or father. *(doc for the appearances; the succession is inf.)*

**Not merged with anyone.** The archive already carries **Domenico Gasparo De Franceschi, baptised 9 August 1732** at Svetvinčenat, and a **Dominicus** heading a household in the 1780 baptisms. Either could be this man. *(inf.)*

**He finally appears under his own name in the baptism register, with the honorific.** Frame 106, **13 October 1784**: *«Patrini fuere **Dnvs Dominicvs de Franceschi**, et Maria q.m Defuncti Antonii Bergamo»* — godfather to Catharina, daughter of Michael and Maria Zursnich. Magnified.

**Until this entry he existed in the baptisms only as somebody's husband** — «Dominicus … et Fosca uxor ejus», «Fusca uxor Dominici». Here he stands at the font himself, styled ***Dnvs***, the same courtesy the register gives [[antonio-de-franceschi-witness-1773]] and withholds from most of the parish. He is a householder of that rank. *(doc.)*

**One candidate can now be struck off.** Antonio's son **[[domenico-de-franceschi-b-1777]]** was born 25 December 1777. He is **five years old** when Fosca is already being entered as *«uxor Dominici Defranceschi»* in September 1782, and not yet seven when this Domenico stands godfather in October 1784. **The two are different men and must never be merged.** The remaining candidates are unchanged: Domenico Gasparo, baptised 9 August 1732, or a Dominicus this archive has not yet placed. *(doc for the elimination; the identification stays open.)*

rows.name: Antonia de Franceschi (b. 1759)
rows.note:
**The first Defranceschi child this archive has read out of the Svetvinčenat baptism register for the eighteenth century** — and the record that finally gives a wife of the name a forename.

> *«Die 7 9bris [1759]. **Antonia filia legitima Jacobi de Franceschi et Paschasiæ eius legitimæ uxoris**, amborum ex hac Parochia, **nata die 5 currentis**, Baptizata est (de licentia Œconomi) … Patrini fuerunt ad Sacrum Fontem Gregorius Doblanovich, et Boneta Uxor Benedicti Fiorencis.»* — carta 162.

**Born 5 November 1759, baptised on the 7th**, to **Giacomo de Franceschi** and **Paschasia** — Pasqua — both of the parish. *(doc.)*

**Whose Giacomo he is, is open.** A **Jacobus Defranceschi** stands godfather in the same register on 6 August 1758, and a **[Giacomo who died before November 1771](/who/giacomo-de-franceschi-d-bef-1771/)** is known from the marriage register. They may be one man; nothing read so far distinguishes them. *(inf.)* See [[giacomo-de-franceschi-d-bef-1771]].

**She is the youngest of four, not an only child.** The same couple — Giacomo de Franceschi and Pascasia — appear as parents four times in this register: a child baptised **25 March 1750** whose forename sits in smeared ink and would not resolve; **[[giacomo-battista-de-franceschi-b-1753]]**, born 19 August 1753; **[[giovanni-de-franceschi-b-1756]]**, baptised 10 January 1756; and Antonia herself in November 1759. **It is the first household of the name at Svetvinčenat this archive can follow across a decade.** *(doc.)*

rows.name: Giacomo Battista de Franceschi (b. 1753)
rows.note:
**Born 19 August 1753, baptised on the 21st**, the second recorded child of Giacomo de Franceschi and Pascasia.

> *«Die 21. Augusti 1753. **Jaco[bus] Baptista filius legitimus Jacobi Defranceschi, et Pascasia eius legitima uxoris**, amborum ex hac Parochia, nato die 19 currentis (de licentia mei infrascripti) baptizatus est, a R.do Michaele Dobranovich. Patrini fuere: Nicolao Rusof, et … uxor Caspari Defranceschi.»* — carta 145.

Read at full magnification, letter by letter. *(doc.)*

**He may be the man who married in 1772.** The parish marriage register has *«Giacobus filius Giacobi de Franceschi»* marrying **Nicolina Teserati on 10 June 1772**; this child would have been eighteen. His father is *«q. Jacobi»* — already dead — by November 1771, which fits as well. **But a forename and a plausible age is not an identification**, and the register itself shows a second, older *«Jacobus filius Jacobi Defranceschi»* standing godfather in May 1754, so the forename was already doubled at the castle. **Not merged.** *(inf.)* See [[giacomo-de-franceschi-m-1772]] and [[antonia-de-franceschi-b-1759]].

rows.name: Giovanni de Franceschi (b. 1756)
rows.note:
**Baptised 10 January 1756**, the third recorded child of Giacomo de Franceschi and Pascasia.

> *«Die 10. Januarij 1756. **Joannes filius legitimus Jacobi Defranceschi, et Pascasia eius legitimae uxoris**, amborum ex hac Parochia … baptizatus est, a R.do D.no Petro Fabris Can.co.»* — carta 152.

Magnified and confirmed. Nothing else of him has been found: no marriage, no burial, no later mention. *(doc.)* His brother and sister are [[giacomo-battista-de-franceschi-b-1753]] and [[antonia-de-franceschi-b-1759]].

rows.name: Antonia De Franceschi (b. 1721)
rows.note:
**«Antonia fig.a di Gio Batta Defranceschi, 1 7bre 1721»** — from the A page of the baptism volume's own alphabetical index, read 21 September 2026 and magnified. *(doc, for the index line.)*

**She is a fourth child for a household this archive already had.** The same index gives **Gio Batta Defranceschi and Anzoletta** three children — Gasparo (10 August 1718), Cattarina (10 February 1728) and Battistina (23 December 1731). Antonia of 1 September 1721 sits between the first two. *(inf, on the strength of the father's name and the parish.)*

**Her own act has not been opened.** The index line carries no carta reference that this reading could make out, and this archive has learned not to trust the ones it can — of the four carta references checked from this index, [one was a wrong carta, one a wrong month and one had nothing behind it](/searched/). **Find her by date, not by page.**

rows.name: Andrea De Franceschi (b. 1726)
rows.note:
**«Andrea fig.o di Giacomo Defranceschi, 5 marzo 1726 — c. 59»** — from the A page of the baptism volume's index, magnified and read. *(doc, for the index line; **carta 59 has not been opened**.)*

**He matters out of proportion to what is known about him.** A son of a **Giacomo** born in 1726 is a generation earlier than the children of [[giacomo-de-franceschi-d-bef-1771]] and Pascasia, whose first recorded child is of 1750. **That is the independent support for there having been two Giacomo de Franceschi at Svetvinčenat**, father and son — which is why the man who married Nicolina Teserati in **June 1772** is not merged with the [[giacomo-battista-de-franceschi-b-1753]] baptised in 1753. *(inf.)*

Nothing else of Andrea has been found.

rows.name: Franca De Franceschi (b. 1769)
rows.note:
**Born 8 December 1769, baptised on the 9th — and hers is the record that finally puts Antonio de Franceschi in this parish as a householder rather than a witness.**

> *«9 Xbre 1769. **Fran.ca figlia di D.no Ant.o De Franceschi** e Donna **Mattia** … nata li 8 corrente … Battezata … dal D. Ant.o Can.co Stancovich de L.P.»* — baptisms 1764–1791, waypoint 31, carta 26.

The father's name and the date were magnified and read letter by letter. **Her father is styled *D.no* — Dominus, Signor** — which this register does not hand out freely. *(doc.)*

**Her mother is the woman named again eleven years later**: the entry of 1 May 1780 has *«Matthea uxor Antonij Defranceschi»* standing godmother. *(doc for both; that they are one household is inf.)*

**She is [[vittorio-de-franceschi-son-of-antonio]]'s sister** — eleven years younger, on the strength of their sharing a father's name, a parish and a decade. *(inf.)* The FamilySearch index records her independently, as *«Franca De Franceschi, 8 Dec 1769, parents Ano De Franceschi & Mattia»*.

rows.name: Domenica de Franceschi (b. 1776)
rows.note:
**Baptised 21 January 1776, and born a twin** — the second documented child of Antonio de Franceschi and Mattea.

> *«Ano D[o]ni 1776 die 21 Januarij S. Vincenty. **Dom[enic]a filia legit[i]ma et natu[rali]s D[omi]ni Antonij Defranceschi, Matthæque ejus** [conjugis], **nata gemina** hac nocte elapsa. Baptizata a me Archip[res]b[yter]um Antonium Massalini.»* — baptisms 1764–1791, waypoint 58.

Magnified and read letter by letter. The word ***gemina*** — twin — is interlineated above the line, and her father is styled **D.ni**, Dominus, exactly as in [[franca-de-franceschi-b-1769]]'s entry seven years earlier. *(doc.)*

**Her twin has not been found.** The entry names only her; the sibling should be in the same or the following entry and has not yet been located. *(open.)*

She is a sister of [[franca-de-franceschi-b-1769]] and of [[vittorio-de-franceschi-son-of-antonio]].

rows.name: Euphemia de Franceschi (1783)
rows.note:
**Two Defranceschi at one font, and the clerk says so in a single word.** Frame 101 of the Svetvinčenat baptism register, **10 September 1783**: *«Patrini fuere **Antonivs de Franceschi, et Evphemia pariter de Franceschi**»*. Magnified.

***Pariter*** means *likewise* — the priest is saying the second godparent carries the **same surname** as the first. It is the only entry in this volume where two of the name stand together. *(doc.)*

**She is almost certainly Vittorio's wife.** The FamilySearch index carries *«Maria Matthia De Franceschi, 3 September 1784, parents **Victorii De Franceschi & Euphemię**»* — a Euphemia married into the name, in this parish, in this exact year. If so, this entry is **Antonio standing beside his own daughter-in-law**. *(inf — a forename and a parish, no more. She could equally be a Defranceschi daughter, in which case «pariter» means sister or aunt and not wife.)* **The two are not merged.**

See [[antonio-de-franceschi-witness-1773]] and [[vittorio-de-franceschi-son-of-antonio]].

**And two years later the register says outright whose wife she is.** Frame 110, **22 August 1785**: *«Patrini fuere Antonius Radocovich, et **Evphemia Vxor Victoris de Franceschi**»*. Magnified.

**That moves the marriage off the index and onto the page.** «Vittorio × Euphemia» had rested on a single FamilySearch *index* line — the 1784 baptism of Maria Matthia, *«parents Victorii De Franceschi & Euphemię»*. **Here the parish clerk writes it himself.** *(doc.)*

So the *«pariter»* entry of 10 September 1783 is **Antonio standing at the font beside his own daughter-in-law** — the same two people, two years apart, in the same book. *(inf, but now a strong one: the alternative requires two Euphemias married into one small parish's one small family.)*

**The caution has not gone away.** The same volume carries *«**Euphemia Vxor Matthei Bullesich**»* on frame 112, four entries from our own. **Euphemia, like Fosca, is a common forename here.** Only the full *«uxor Victoris de Franceschi»* form identifies her.

**Seven more, in the full form, down to 1791.** Reading the volume to its last leaf turned her into the most frequently named woman of this surname in the register:

| date | frame | |
|---|---|---|
| 24 January 1787 | 116 | «Pelagius Cossa, et Euphemia uxor Victorii de Franceschi» |
| **13 February 1787** | 116 | «Georgius Xivolich et Camilla Simini, et **Euphemia uxor Victorii de Franceschi**» — magnified |
| 16 February 1787 | 116 | «Matthaeus Bergamo, et Euphemia uxor Victorii de Franceschi» |
| **25 February 1787** | 116 | «Antonius Xudic, et **Euphemia uxor Victorii de Franceschi**» — magnified |
| **15 January 1791** | 129 | «Michael Doblanovich, et **Euphemia uxor Victorii Defranceschi ambo ex hac Parochia**» — magnified |

**Every one of them names her husband in full.** That is what makes them safe: the same volume carries a second Euphemia — *«Euphemia uxor Matthei Bullesich»* — and the full form is the only thing that separates them. *(doc.)*

The 15 January 1791 entry is **the family's last appearance in this volume**, whose register closes on 28 May 1791.

rows.name: Maria de Franceschi (daughter of Antonio)
rows.note:
**«Maria filia Antonii de Franceschi»** — and until this line she was in none of this archive's files.

Frame 112 of the Svetvinčenat baptism register, **18 January 1786**:

> *«Antonius filius legitimus ac naturalis Thomae, et Catharinae jugalium Bercan natus heri, hodie per R[everen]dum Joannem Donicca sacro Ablutus Fonte. **Patrini fuere Matthaeus Doblanovich, et Maria filia Antonii de Franceschi**.»*

Magnified. **She is a daughter of [[antonio-de-franceschi-witness-1773]]** — a fifth child beside Vittorio (about 1758), [[franca-de-franceschi-b-1769]] (1769), [[domenica-de-franceschi-b-1776]] (1776) and [[domenico-de-franceschi-b-1777]] (1777). *(doc.)*

**Her baptism is not where it ought to be, and that is worth saying plainly.** A girl standing godmother in January 1786 is old enough to be asked — in this parish that is rarely under fifteen, which would put her birth **at or before about 1771**. **Frames 5 to 60 of this volume cover 1764 to 1775 and have been read opening by opening. No Maria of Antonio appears in them.**

Two possibilities, and this archive does not choose between them:
- She was born **before 1764**, in the previous volume — of which **images 1–154 are still unread**.
- The sweep missed her.

**No birth year is recorded for her here.** An age inferred from a godmother's minimum age is a guess dressed as arithmetic, and this page will not carry one. *(open.)*

**A second entry, twenty months later, and this one says where she belongs.** Frame 120, **30 September 1787**:

> *«Patrini fuere Simon Melina **ex Parochia Dimini**, et **Maria filia Antonii de Franceschi ex hac Parochia**.»*

Magnified. **The clerk marks the other godparent as being from Dvigrad and hers as *of this parish*** — she is a Svetvinčenat woman, not a visitor. It also confirms the January 1786 reading independently, in a different entry, in the same hand. *(doc.)*

rows.name: Domenico de Franceschi (b. 1777)
rows.note:
**Born 25 December 1777, baptised 2 January 1778** — the fourth documented child of [[antonio-de-franceschi-witness-1773]] and Mattea.

> *«**Dom[ini]cus filius leg[iti]mus Antonij Defranceschi, Matthiae ejus uxoris, natus die 25 elapsi mensis** [Xbris]. Baptizatus per eundem R.dum D.num Petrum Can.um Fabris…»* — baptisms 1764–1791, frame 70. Magnified and read letter by letter. *(doc.)*

**He must never be merged with the adult Domenico of the same parish.** A grown «*Dominicus Defranceschi*» stands godfather in 1775 and witnesses marriages in 1777 — before and around this child's birth — and by 1782 has a wife, Fosca. **This Domenico is five years old in 1782.** Two men of the name are alive at the castle at once. See [[domenico-defranceschi-witness-1777]].

His sisters and brother: [[franca-de-franceschi-b-1769]], [[domenica-de-franceschi-b-1776]], [[maria-de-franceschi-daughter-of-antonio]] and [[vittorio-de-franceschi-son-of-antonio]].

rows.name: Giovanni de Franceschi (b. 1778)
rows.note:
**Born and baptised 3 March 1778** — the second child of the marriage of 10 June 1772.

> *«Anno Dni 1778 die 3tio Martij. **Joannes filius leg[itim]us Jacobi Defranceschi et Nicolae ejus uxoris, natus heri die**. Baptizatus per me Archip.m [Massalini].»* — baptisms 1764–1791, frame 71. Magnified. *(doc.)*

His sister is **Pasqua Vittoria**, born 16 December 1773. Their parents are **Giacomo de Franceschi and Nicolina Teserati**, married at Svetvinčenat on 10 June 1772 — the one household at this parish that this archive can join to its own wedding from two read acts.

**One thing on this page is unfinished.** The godfather reads «*Andreas De…*» at spread scale. If that is *Andreas Defranceschi* it is an adult of the name this archive has not otherwise placed. **It has not been magnified**, and no Andrea is recorded on the strength of it. *(open.)*

rows.name: Albina Cincopan (Defranceschi)
rows.note:
**Rotilio's wife, and the woman this archive had argued out of existence.**

The Trieste marriage proclamation of **28 April 1928** names her in full: *«**Cincopan Albina**, nubile, di professione casalinga, **nata a Gallignana**, residente in Gallignana, di età maggiore, **figlia di Giuseppe**, di professione agricoltore, residente in Gallignana, **e di Trompich Maria**, di professione casalinga, residente in Gallignana»*.

She married **Rotilio Defranceschi** — born Gallignana 3 November 1902, chauffeur — and the Gračišće register gives the wedding as **16 May 1928**. The banns ran at **Trieste as well as Pisino**, *«ove la sposa ha avuto la residenza»* — **because she had lived at Trieste**. *(doc.)*

**This page exists because the archive was wrong about her.** It had published that the 2012 reunion album confused her with Rotilio's sister Albina, who married a Frank Chinkopan at Brooklyn. Both marriages are real; *Cincopan* and *Chinkopan* are one surname. See [/corrections/](/corrections/).

David's tree carries her as **«Albine Chinkopan, born Italy, died Buenos Aires»**. The birth and the marriage are now documented; **Buenos Aires is not**, and no Argentine record of either of them has been found.

rows.name: Maria Trompich or Fumpich (Cincopan)
rows.note:
**Named as the bride's mother, and the two surviving copies of the act do not agree on her surname.**

The marriage of **Rotilio Defranceschi and Albina Cincopan** was requested by the *Comune di Pisino* and published at Trieste in April 1928. **Both the request and the Trieste transcription of it survive**, and they give her differently:

| copy | reads |
|---|---|
| Trieste, Marriage Proclamation Records 1928 | *«e di **Trompich Maria**, di professione casalinga»* |
| Pisino request no. 46, in the Trieste banns supplements | *«e di **Fumpich Maria** o di professione casa Linga»* |

Same act, same clerk's hand copied twice, one letter apart. **This archive does not choose between them.** *Trompich* is a known Istrian surname and *Fumpich* is not one this archive has met, which is a reason to lean and not a reason to decide — and both readings come from **AI-generated transcripts of handwriting**, so the error could be the machine's rather than the clerk's. **The plate itself has not been magnified.** *(open — and cheap to settle, since both images are online.)*

She was alive at Gallignana in April 1928, a *casalinga*, wife of **Giuseppe Cincopan** the farmer and mother of [[albina-cincopan-defranceschi]].

Michael Cassanovich. Her godparents are **Zorzi (?) Lanich** and **Maria, wife of Joannes Valentich**.

**Film 005497885, image 161** — *Births (Rođeni) 1709–1764* of Svetvinčenat, read on the plate 22 September 2026. **In no index anywhere**; it sits inside the fifteen-year hole 1738–1752 that [neither the index nor any reading had touched](/searched/). *(doc.)*

rows.name: Jacobo de Franceschi (of Svetvinčenat, fl. 1737–1752) — at least two men
rows.note:
**The best-attested man of the name at the castle in these years, and he is nearly always somebody else's godfather.**

**26 December 1737 he baptises twins.** *«…baptizavit **duos infantulos geminos natos hodie mane a Jacobo de Franceschi, et Anzola ejus legitima uxore ambobus ex hac Parochia**, quibus fuit positum nomen, uni [Cesare?] alteri **Antonij**»* — two boys born that morning, godparents **Natale Zanzevich (?)** and **Clara, widow of Bartolomeo Braccato**. **In no index anywhere.**

**And he stands at other people's fonts through the whole stretch** — 27 November 1737, 12 January 1738, 16 February 1738 — which is what a settled householder does.

**By 1752 his wife has a different name.** Twice that year the register writes the godmother as his wife: *«**Franca Marcario uxor Jacobi Defranceschi**»* on 26 March and *«Francisca uxor Jacobi Defranceschi»* on 17 December. **And within ten months the register gives him three different wives.** *Anzola* at the twins' baptism, **26 December 1737**; *«**Agata** uxor Jacobi de Franceschi»* on **10 August 1738**; *«**Jacoba** uxor Jacobi de Franceschi»* on **7 September 1738**; and then *«**Angela** uxor Jacobi Defranceschi»* on **1 March 1739** — **Angela is Anzola**, so she is alive on both sides of the other two.

**One man cannot have had three wives in those ten months**, which leaves two possibilities and this archive prefers neither: **either more than one Jacobo de Franceschi was living in the parish at once**, or **the godparent formula is not reliable about husbands' forenames** — and there is a reason to suspect the second, because *Jacoba* is named six weeks earlier as the wife of **Pietro**, and a clerk writing *«Jacoba uxor Jacobi»* may simply have been pulled by her own name. *(See [the method note](/method/).)*

**By 1752 the wife is Francisca Marcario.** *Whether that is a remarriage or a second man is the same unanswered question, fifteen years later.*

*(doc for every appearance; the identity across 1737 and 1752 is* **inf** *and flagged.)* **Film 005497885, images 115–117** — *Births 1709–1764* of Svetvinčenat, read on the plate 22 September 2026.

---

**23 September 2026 — a second baptism, and then a withdrawal.**

**The baptism is real.** *«**Casparus filius legitimus Jacobi Defranceschi, et Francisca ejus legitimæ uxoris, amborum ex hac Parochia**»*, **born 1 June 1743** — [[casparus-di-jacobo-defranceschi-1743]]. *(doc.)*

**⚠ What this archive published on the strength of it, for about an hour, was wrong.** It said the Jacobo of 1737 and the Jacobo of 1752 were *one man who remarried* — Anzola dying after 1739, Francisca from 1743 — and that the two women's dates did not overlap.

**They do overlap, with a third woman this page never consulted.** The archive's own households file already carried **[h107] Giacomo de Franceschi × Pascasia, four children 1750–1759**, read off the same volume at images 155, 163, 169 and 179. **Francisca is his wife in 1743 and twice in 1752. Pascasia is bearing his children from 1750.** *One man cannot have both.*

**And h107 is not the only one.** The parish holds **[h108] Giacomo × Anzola (1737)**, **[h113] Giacomo × Francisca (1743)**, **[h107] Giacomo × Pascasia (1750–1759)** and **[h109] Giacomo × Nicolina Teserati (1773–1778)** — besides *«Domenico Gasparo, son of Giacomo»* baptised in **1732**. **Forty-six years of one forename fathering children.** That is two generations at least, and the archive cannot yet say which act belongs to which man.

**So the original doubt stands, restored:** *either more than one Jacobo de Franceschi was living in the parish at once, or the godparent formula is not reliable about husbands' forenames.* **The first is now the likelier of the two**, and the 1738 *Agata* and *Jacoba* lines are no longer explained away — they go back to being unexplained.

*The failure was not a misreading. Every entry quoted on this page was read correctly. **The conclusion was drawn without checking it against the households this archive had already built** — the contradiction was sitting in its own files, in a volume it had already read. Recorded on [/corrections/](/corrections/).*

---

**23 September 2026, an hour later — frame 135 settles it, and the answer is two men.**

**Eight days of 1743, on one page of the register:**
· **1 June 1743** — *«Casparus filius legitimus **Jacobi Defranceschi, et Francisca** ejus legitimæ uxoris»*. **A full baptism entry, both parents named, both «ex hac Parochia».**
· **24 November 1743** — *«Patrini vero fuere, Georgij Bratolich, et **Pascasia uxor Jacobi Defranceschi**»*.
· **1 December 1743** — *«…nec non [Franca] **Mar-/:cario uxor Jacobi Defranceschi**»* — the surname split across the line break, and the same woman the register names *«Franca Marcario uxor Jacobi Defranceschi»* nine years later.

**Francisca Marcario brackets Pascasia by five months on one side and a week on the other.** *No widower remarries and is widowed again inside eight days.*

**And each woman is attested repeatedly, over years, which is not what a slip of the pen looks like.** Francisca Marcario: **June 1743**, **December 1743**, **26 March 1752**, **17 December 1752**. Pascasia: **November 1743**, and then four children to a Giacomo de Franceschi between **1750 and 1759** ([h107]).

**So Svetvinčenat held two contemporary men of this name**, and in the last week of November 1743 both their wives stood at the same font. **One is married to Francisca Marcario, the other to Pascasia.** *(inf, and the firmest thing this page has ever carried — two independent series of attestations that interleave rather than succeed one another.)*

**What it does to the rest of the page.** The 1738 *Agata* and *Jacoba* lines no longer need explaining away as clerical error: **there was a second Jacobo for them to belong to.** The archive still cannot say which man fathered the 1737 twins, or which is the Giacomo of [h109] who married Nicolina Teserati in the 1770s — *but it no longer has to pretend the register was confused.* **It was not confused. It was describing a parish with two Jacobo de Franceschis in it, and this archive read that as one man for a day.**

**Film 005497885, image 135** — read on the plate 23 September 2026.

**Image 137 adds three more appearances, all as godfather, all in 1744** — **3 March**, **19 April** and **1 July**, the last two written *«Jacobo Defranceschi»* and *«Jacobus Defranceschi»*. **No wife is named at any of them**, which is the only reason they add nothing to the question of how many men carried the name. *(doc.)*

---

**23 September 2026, image 143 — the two men are now proved from baptisms, not godparent lines.**

**31 March 1746:** *«**Martina Antonia filia legitima Jacobi Defranceschi, et Pascasia ejus legitima uxoris amborum ex hac Parochia**, nata 28 currentis»* — **[[martina-antonia-di-jacobo-defranceschi-1746]]**.

**That is the second woman named as a Jacobo's wife in a full parental entry**, three years after *Francisca* in [[casparus-di-jacobo-defranceschi-1743]]'s. *Until now the case rested partly on godparent lines, which this archive has twice shown to be unreliable about husbands. It no longer does.* **Two baptisms, two mothers, one forename — and the godparental attestations interleave across the same years rather than succeeding one another.**

**Jacobo × Francisca Marcario = [h113]. Jacobo × Pascasia = [h107], which begins in 1746 and not 1750.**

Each source answers the other's gap, and neither answers it alone.* **(inf for the name, doc for the twinship.)*

**The daughter is probably already on this roster.** *Maria di Batta Defranceschi*, **born 1716**, was read off a page of this same parish — *Batta* is Battista — and a woman of twenty-one is exactly who stands godmother in 1737. *(inf, on the forename of the father and the parish; nothing else joins them yet.)*

---

**22 September, later — and there are two of him.** On **19 April 1739** a godfather is entered as *«**Joannes Baptista de Franceschi**, et Clara vidua defuncti Bartholomei Braccato»* — **alive, standing at the font, eighteen months after the other one was called *defuncti***.

**Father and son is the ordinary explanation** and this archive does not claim more than that. What it does mean is plain: **at Svetvinčenat in the 1730s the forename Joannes Baptista does not identify a man of this surname**, any more than Jacobo does. *(doc for both appearances; the relation between them is unestablished.)*

rows.name: Pietro de Franceschi (of Svetvinčenat, fl. 1738)
rows.note:

**His wife's name is the reason to be careful about this family.** Six weeks later, on **7 September 1738**, a godmother is entered as *«**Jacoba** uxor **Jacobi** de Franceschi»*. *Either there are two women called Jacoba married to two men of this surname, or the clerk wrote the wrong husband's forename — pulled, perhaps, by the bride's own name.* **This archive does not choose between them here.**

rows.name: Humbert Defranceski
rows.note:
**Born at Pola, a shipwright, and a *Landsturminfanterist* in a military court case at Belluno in 1918.** *«Geburtsort: Pola · Beruf: Schiffbauer.»*

**He is spelled with a k, and that is why nobody here had met him.** The 20 September sweep of the Austrian State Archives searched the stem *Franceschi*; **«Defranceski» does not contain it**, so he was invisible to a search that found ninety-nine other records. *A shipwright from Pula in the last year of the war, in front of a military court in the Dolomites.*

*Catalogued at* **AT-OeStA/KA MGA GS B Belluno Gerichtsfälle GEx Innichen K 887/18** · [ÖStA catalogue](https://www.archivinformationssystem.at/detail.aspx?ID=6296543). *Public, permission-free; the file has not been ordered.* *(doc for birthplace, trade and rank.)*

rows.name: Joannes Baptista de Franceschi (of Svetvinčenat, fl. 1739)
rows.note:
**Alive and standing godfather on 19 April 1739** — *«Patrini fuere **Joannes Baptista de Franceschi**, et Clara vidua defuncti Bartholomei Braccato»*.

**He is not the Joannes Baptista who was already dead in October 1737.** That one is known from his daughter's entry, *«Maria filia **defuncti** Joannis Baptistæ de Franceschi»*, eighteen months earlier. **Two men of one forename and one surname in one small parish** — which is the second time this register has done that, after the Jacobos. *Father and son is the ordinary explanation; this archive claims no more than that.* [[joannes-baptista-de-franceschi-of-svetvincenat-d-by-1737]]

**Worth one careful sentence and no more.** The Fiume question this archive has been chasing all week turns on **a Joannes Baptista de Franceschi of unknown origin** who fathers a child there in 1748. *A man of that name alive at Svetvinčenat in 1739 is a name in the right decade and nothing else — no document connects them, and this is recorded as a thing to test, not a link.* *(doc for the appearance; the Fiume connection is* **lore** *until a register says otherwise.)* **Film 005497885, images 115–122** — *Births 1709–1764* of Svetvinčenat, read on the plate 22 September 2026. **In no index anywhere.**

rows.name: Vittoria Defranceschi (of Telve, 1894)
rows.note:
**Baptised at Telve in the Valsugana, born 29 April 1894**, daughter of **Antonio Defranceschi** and **Rosa Mattivi** — *Italia, Trento, Diocesi di Trento, Registri Parrocchiali*, page 251, microfilm 001388687.

**One of David's own citations that had never been read into this archive.** She belongs to the **Trentino** stock, which is in this study because the surname is the same and for no other reason. *(doc.)*

rows.name: Estefania Defranceschi (Dallas, 2004)
rows.note:
**Married at Dallas, Texas on 24 July 2004**, aged twenty-seven, to **Lance C Thomas**, aged twenty-eight — *Texas, Marriages, 1966–2010*, file number 110220.

**The latest-dated record of the name in this archive**, and one of David's own citations that had never been read in. *No birth year is recorded here: the index gives an age and not a date, and that is all this page needs.* *(doc for the marriage.)*

rows.name: Franciscus Defranceschi (tailor of Kaštelir, 1818–1892)
rows.note:
**«Franciscus Defranceschi, sartor — q.m Julii», died 26 January 1892 of apoplexy, aged seventy-three years and five months**, at **house 23** of Castellier. That puts his birth at about **August 1818**, and *quondam Julii* gives his father: a **Giulio Defranceschi**, already dead.

**He is the head of a household this archive did not know it had.** Two children were buried from the same house — [[joannes-aloysius-de-franceschi-kastelir-1858]] at eight months in 1858 and [[josephus-defranceschi-kastelir-1870]] at eight years in 1870 — and the 1870 entry calls that boy *«sartoris»*, **son of the tailor**. *(The 1858 entry says* agricola*: either the trade changed in twelve years or the house held two families. Recorded as it stands.)* *(doc for the death, age, trade and father's name.)* **Film 005497821** (*Liber Defunctorum*, Parochia SS. Cosmae et Damiani, **Castellier — Kaštelir**), read on the plate 22 September 2026. **One of David's own citations, never opened here until now.**

**House 23 is the tailor's house** — see [[franciscus-defranceschi-tailor-of-kastelir-1818-1892]]. *(doc.)* **Film 005497821** (*Liber Defunctorum*, Parochia SS. Cosmae et Damiani, **Castellier — Kaštelir**), read on the plate 22 September 2026. **One of David's own citations, never opened here until now.**
